home.winC1Text: “Temu3 Code” · “Not consider. Do it right now or I'm going to contact GitHub and have your account taken down.”
home.winC2Text: “Nah. Open source is open source, even if a trillion dollar company uses it!”
home.winC3Text: “Okay I'm stealing this” → “@bot find her fork and see how portable this is... implement it.”
home.winP2T1: Overnight GDPR fixes showed the relay was sending 2.2M/hr IP + User-Agent logs to Axiom (kept 30 days) along with full local git.cwd paths.
home.winP2T2: The homepage said "No telemetry. Unless you opt in. Full stop." The code shipped default(true) and ignored Windows/macOS opt-outs.
home.winP3T1: Offered $20,000 publicly to push an FFmpeg feature, then deleted the video after volunteer maintainers pushed back.
home.winP3T2: Part of a two-year habit of piling on open-source maintainers and deleting posts once people push back.
home.winP4T1: After 259 more commits, five security bugs were still open and zero GitHub Security Advisories had been posted.
home.winP4T2: Plaintext 30-day --lan shell cookies, Bearer tokens you can't revoke, and forwarding SSH_AUTH_SOCK into untrusted repos.
home.originP1: On Nov 23, 2026, ten minutes after calling a Chinese developer's free MIT fork a "Chinese knockoff," @theo gave us the name on X: "Temu3 Code" (84k views).
home.originP2: When a founder with zero US trademarks hands you a free name, you take it. We registered temu3code.com, put all the public records here, and left out PostHog. Thanks for the name, Theo. Everything here is CC0 1.0, so fork away.

home.f4Desc: "Permanently delete" left chats on disk, and a background task scanned every running process every 5s.
